messages:
jen: quick status — ran two comparison suites this morning: synthetic (uniform prompt lengths) and replay (prod traces from 2026-03). putting notes here for kernel/batching/KV cache differences.

mike: nice, can you paste the config you used? especially batch cap and max delay.

jen: sure — config snippet:
```
batch_cap: 64
max_delay_ms: 8
policy: continuous
kernel_selector: auto (float16 -> int8 fallback)
kv_cache_prefetch: enabled
kv_cache_warmup_window: 60s
```

arya: what model size? that changes ETT and kernel choices.

jen: 13B fp16 baseline, with a quantized int8 variant for fallback.

tom: TL;DR numbers? throughput / p50 / p95?

jen: paste of distilled results (avg across 6 runs):
- synthetic: throughput 128 req/s, p50 22ms, p95 110ms, kv-hit 4%
- replay: throughput 92 req/s, p50 28ms, p95 210ms, kv-hit 46%

liz: interesting p95 gap — replay has higher p95 despite kv hits being higher. could be queueing spikes from variable seq lengths.

mike: kernel_selector auto might be switching kernels mid-run. can you share profiler traces? i want to see kernel swap frequency + stall time.

jen: uploaded flame snippet: https://redwood-gists/internal/bench/212345 — but paste small excerpt:
```
[00:01:12] kernel_select: conv_fused -> fast_attention_int8 (swap_count=12)
[00:01:14] stall_ms: 38 (waiting for int8 kernel init)
[00:01:14] kv_cache_lookup_ms: +6ms/req
```

arya: that stall is worrying. if kernel init happens on the hot path it blows p95. we usually pre-select kernel or warm kernels during startup for known sequence length buckets.

jen: right — I tried preloading kernels but it increased memory footprint and sometime caused OOM in the dedicated pool.

mike: two followups: (1) validate kernel init is lazy only for int8 path, (2) add lightweight pre-warm: spawn one dummy request per kernel variant before traffic. should be cheap.

perf-bot: smoke results after warmup run #7:
- kernels warmed: conv_fused, fast_attention_fp16, fast_attention_int8
- dummy init time: 82ms total
- p95 improved by ~12% on synthetic, ~9% on replay

tom: good. how about batching heuristics — is the continuous policy accumulating cross-tenant requests that skew fairness?

jen: replay includes 12 tenants. observed tenant-skew: top 2 tenants get 65% of CPU time due to more short-sequence traffic which groups faster. middle tenants see higher queueing delays.

liz: batching favors high-arrival-rate tenants because of queueing; fairness levers we tried: per-tenant batch caps and tenant-weighted delay cap. did you run those?

jen: ran two quick experiments:
- per-tenant batch_cap: 32 (global 64) => overall throughput -6%, tail latency improved for small tenants by ~28%
- tenant-weighted delay (max_delay_ms=8 -> per-tenant cap min 2ms for low qps) => fairness improved but throughput unstable under microbursts

mike: tradeoff expected. maybe an adaptive delay cap that uses ETT-estimate per tenant: ETT = avg_token_time * expected_seq_len. bound max_delay by alpha * ETT.

arya: agree. also KV cache behavior: replay shows 46% hits but hit distribution skewed — top tenant accounts for 70% of hits. When top tenant bursts, cache thrashing evicts useful entries for other tenants.

jen: saw that — eviction logs: LRU churn spikes during burst windows.

mike: two practical experiments to run next: (A) LRU shard per-tenant (soft partition) to prevent cross-tenant eviction, (B) TTL-based pinning for high-value prefixes. run both with identical replay slices for apples-to-apples comparison.

liz: +1 for controlled slices. also keep kernel warm strategy identical across experiments. we need consistent seeds.

jen: noted. planning to run 8-hour harness with 10-min rolling windows. will pin seed, kernel warm, and run: baseline, per-tenant-batchcap, adaptive-delay, kv-shard, kv-ttl.

perf-bot: scheduled job 2123456789-1 (harness) queued on staging pool. estimated runtime 9h. link: https://ci.redwood/internal/jobs/2123456789-1

mike: when results are in, create a condensed CSV with columns: experiment, throughput, p50, p95, p99, kv_hit_global, kv_hit_median_by_tenant, cpu_util, kernel_swap_count, OOMs.

jen: will do. one more oddity: we saw a perf regression on latest runtime build (r2.14.0 -> r2.15.1). p95 went +18% on replay only. profiler shows increased memcpy cost in KV lookup path.

arya: that could be a side-effect of a recent buffer-copy patch (PR #4456). @mike can you bisect?

mike: starting bisect now. suspect change in kv lookup API that converts small views to owned buffers on certain alignment. low-prob but plausible.

sre-bot: alert — r2.15.1 rollout paused in staging due to increased tail latency on perf harness. rollback candidate r2.14.3.

jen: thanks. I'll hold the big 8h run until we confirm bisect. in parallel I'll change harness to capture per-tenant eviction traces and kernel-init timestamps so we can correlate evictions -> kernel swaps -> p95 spikes.

tom: add a small synthetic microburst test too (10s 5x rate) to see how delay cap and per-tenant caps behave under burst. that's where fairness often breaks.

jen: added. I'll post a short summary thread after the runs with CSV and recommendations. tagging @mike @arya for visibility. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks — will follow up with bisect results by EOD.

arya: if bisect pins to buffer-copy patch, we should patch to avoid copies for aligned slices and ship a hotfix.

perf-bot: note: job 2123456789-1 started 2123456810

jen: got it. ttyl.
